text:
Maya: Quick flag 10: Legal handed us a privacy request this morning asking us to prove deletion of derived vectors (embeddings + cached prefixes). They want an auditable proof chain that covers primary objects, cross-region snapshots, and any ephemeral GPU cache. Thoughts on approach?
Jin: Short take: two separate proofs: (A) canonical deletion receipt for primary store (S3/GCS) and (B) manifest + vendor-ack for snapshots/backups. For GPU/ram caches we can only assert ttl/eviction and include service logs showing cache flush ops.
Priya: Agree. For primary store we can emit an "erasure_receipt" which is a signed statement containing request_id, object_paths, sha256s, delete_op_id, operator, and key_id. Keep receipts immutable in a write-once Audit bucket. Avoid storing PII in the receipt payload.
Sarah (Legal): That seems promising. Legal will accept a signed receipt + reasonable explanation for ephemeral caches. For vendor-managed snapshots we need a formal retention-exception process and an estimate when the subject's data will be redacted or purged. Also include approver metadata.
Maya: Two infra constraints: (1) our KMS rotates keys nightly and sometimes the signing key is temporarily disabled during rotation, (2) cross-region snapshot delete APIs are limited and require an elevated role. We need a workable fallback so we don't miss SLAs on DSARs.
Jin: Fallback pattern: create an append-only tombstone record in Audit bucket immediately with fields: request_id, object_paths, hashes, deletion_state = "pending_sign" and retention_exception = boolean. Mark tombstone with server-side encryption using KMS but do NOT require immediate key signing. Once KMS signs, attach signature and change deletion_state to "signed". All ops produce events (kafka/audit-log) so chain-of-custody is visible.
Priya: For RBAC, propose a narrowly-scoped role `privacy-erasure-lite` with permissions: s3:DeleteObject (prefix-scoped), snapshots:DeleteSnapshot (specific resource pattern), logging:WriteAudit. Create an emergency flow to allow time-limited elevation (15m) with two-person approval. We'll gate cross-region deletes behind that.
Maya: Can we make tombstones tamper-evident without KMS signature? I want to avoid legal claims that we retroactively changed tombstones.
Jin: Use S3 versioning + object-lock (governance mode) for Audit bucket. Tombstone upload will be done with object-lock retain-until-date far future and with server-side kms encryption. That prevents object deletion or overwrite; metadata can still be appended as new object versions. Also log uploader identity and write sha256 over tombstone payload. Later signed receipt references the tombstone version id.
infra-bot: :warning: KMS key rotation window scheduled 3125010100-3125010200 for keys/erasure-signing-key. See infra runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-signing-rotation
Priya: Additional edge: if rotation overlaps DSAR, the tombstone approach means we can still meet the response deadline by sending the user a "pending" acknowledgement. Legal guidance: include expected timeframe and that a signed receipt will follow.
Sarah (Legal): Confirmed: user notification + documented retention-exception justification + approver details required. If the request is urgent we should offer a human-readable interim notice and follow-up signed proof. Also require playbook entry for when a vulnerability triage places data under legal_hold; that must block deletion and link to request_id.
Maya: Good point re: legal_hold. For vuln triage we need a signal from sec-triage that creates legal_hold=true on the tombstone record and notifies Privacy queue. That should be auditable.
Jin: Implementation notes:
- Tombstone schema is a single-line JSON string (no PII) uploaded as s3://redwood-audit/erasure-tombstones/{request_id}.json
- Tombstone fields: request_id, objects[], hashes[], deletion_state, created_ts, created_by, hold_id (optional), retention_exception (bool)
- Signed receipt: sign(canonicalize(tombstone_version_id||"|"||created_ts||"|"||request_id)) using asymmetric KMS key. Store signature alongside tombstone as .sig object.
- Verification: fetch tombstone + signature + KMS public key; verify signature matches.
Example tombstone payload (single-line): {"request_id":"req-20260321-vec-01","objects":["s3://eu-embeddings/vec_7b9"],"hashes":["5d41402abc4b2a76b9719d911017c592"],"deletion_state":"pending_sign","created_ts":"2026-03-21T09:45:00Z","created_by":"privacy-service"}

Priya: Tests: unit test for canonicalization, e2e for rotation-window, and an integration test that simulates legal_hold preventing delete and emitting hold_id. Also add an alert when tombstone remains pending > SLA (72h by default).
Maya: Operational: update runbooks: DSAR flow, retention-exception form, legal_hold linking, and RBAC elevation steps. Priya please draft the minimal IAM policy and the elevation play.
Priya: Will do. Draft policy snippet: ```json
{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Statement":[{
    "Effect":"Allow",
    "Action":["s3:DeleteObject","s3:PutObject","snapshots:DeleteSnapshot"],
    "Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-eu/embeddings/*","arn:aws:snapshots:eu:*:snapshot/*"]
  }]
}```Policy will be scoped further in PR.
Sarah (Legal): Please include a retention-exception template that captures: owner, approver, reason, expected purge date, communication plan, and legal_hold link. I'll draft language.
Maya: Let's meet 30m after standup to align owners. I'll open tracking tickets for tombstones, IAM, runbooks, and tests. Keep this thread as the record.
Jin: I'll push a prototype (tombstone writer + signature verifier) to infra: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pulls soon.
Priya: Pinged.
Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll close with action items in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
